newsitem.title: MEXICO: GMexico Q1 hurt by prices, bottleneck.
newsitem.headline: GMexico Q1 hurt by prices, bottleneck.

text.p: Mexico's largest mining firm Grupo Mexico SA (GMexico) posted slightly disappointing first quarter results that show the company was hurt by relatively weak copper and zinc prices, analysts said.
GMexico reported a first quarter net profit of 594.85 million pesos, down some 32 percent on profits during the year-ago quarter.
Earnings were 0.86 pesos per share, slightly below the 0.92 pesos per share forecast for the quarter in a Reuters' survey of four industry analysts.
Analysts said results looked better compared to the fourth quarter of last year, when copper and zinc prices were at even lower levels.
Since prices for both commodities had still not recovered to their first quarter 1996 levels, however, it made the results look poor on a year-to-year basis.
They added that a strong peso during the quarter artificially hurt the company, which earns most of its revenues in dollars but has to report earnings in inflation-adjusted pesos.

"You can produce the same, sell the same, and earn the same amount of dollars, but if the peso is strong, then that determines what your earnings are," said David Bodenberg, an analyst at Credit Lyonnais.

But other analysts said GMexico hurt itself by not producing the same amount of copper, its main product, and zinc to take advantage of the rebound in those commodities' prices from fourth quarter lows.

"The results were generally good but their sales volume was down in the quarter, which is a shame because there were pretty good copper and zinc prices," said Christopher Albi, a mining analyst at Valores Finamex in Mexico City.
Copper prices during the quarter were up 12.9 percent compared to the fourth quarter, but still down 5.8 percent from the first quarter of 1996, Albi said.
But GMexico produced 7.8 percent less copper during the quarter compared to the fourth quarter and 9.8 percent less than the year-ago quarter, he added.
Albi said the company's output was hurt by a bottleneck in getting an expansion at its La Caridad unit fully operational during the quarter.
Albi added the bottleneck was a one-time incident and the company should be able to boost output in the second quarter.
"The plant should soon be at full capacity," he said.
Other analysts agreed. "Any decrease in net profits at the company can't be seen as a reflection of management," Bodenberg said.
GMexico's margin was better than expected at 35.8 percent and the company managed to further draw down its debt by paying off $52 million in bank debt, analysts said.
